Open org ownership.
For Lakeshore Holdings, org ownership across IT is structurally split — and that split is intentional, not a gap.
• Corporate IT ($36.5M) owns shared services and enterprise platforms at the holdco level; four named operating companies carry their own local IT budgets totaling $154.1M — meaning roughly 81% of IT spend lives outside central control.
• That decentralization is a governance risk at scale: with $7.12B in portfolio revenue and 11,800 employees, inconsistent ownership over ERP, HCM, treasury, and contract lifecycle creates compounding audit and integration exposure across the portfolio.
• The active build and pilot programs — Corporate ERP/HCM modernization, Treasury cash visibility, Legal contract lifecycle, and Portfolio data foundation — are the clearest leverage points for rebalancing ownership before the decentralized model hardens further.
No named ownership gaps are surfaced in current business context, but operating company attribution for the $3.56B unallocated revenue bucket warrants validation before ownership decisions are finalized.
Branch: **Tower** for budget authority and value decisions · **Moves** for sequencing the four active programs · **Intelligence** for holdco-vs-opco governance tradeoffs · **Source** for any vendor or platform ownership questions.
